newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Ranariddh residence, French embassy heavily damage.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh residence, French embassy heavily damage.

text.p: The residence of Cambodia's First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh and the French embassy were badly damaged by shelling on Sunday as forces under Second Prime Minister Hun Sen tightened their grip on the city, officials said.

The fighting between forces loyal to the two prime ministers began on Saturday and by Sunday afternoon troops loyal to Hun Sen were moving through the city street by street as heavy fighting continued around pockets of Ranariddh's men holed up in some key areas.
Military officials loyal to Hun Sen said they were demanding the surrender of Ranariddh's troops protecting some of his facilities. A general loyal to the prince said there would be no surrender.

At least 12 people have been killed and more than 50 wounded since the violence began on Saturday, hospital sources and local news reports said. An official at one hospital said medical supplies would start running out if the fighting continued much longer.

The heaviest fighting raged around key facilities under the control of forces loyal to Ranariddh, including a well-defended compound, a base near the international airport, Ranariddh's party headquarters and his residence -- all of which were protected by security men and troops.

Thousands of people streamed out of the city on Sunday as the fighting raged. Ranariddh has accused Hun Sen of trying to stage a coup, but a radio station controlled by Hun Sen denied the accusations.
